canonical_name: Voldman 2006 — Electrical forces for microscale cell manipulation (Annual Reviews of Biomed Eng)
creator: Joel Voldman
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1146/annurev.bioeng.8.061505.095739; Annu. Rev. Biomed. Eng. 8, 425-454 (2006)
prior_art_notes: Annual Reviews chapter cataloguing electrical methods (DEP, EP, electroosmosis, electrowetting, electroporation) for cell manipulation in microfluidic devices. Anticipates: any single-cell platform patent that claims electrical force as its manipulation principle without further inventive distinction — the catalog of electrical-force modalities for cells was published in 2006. Particularly load-bearing for DEP-trap, EP-sorter, and EWOD-cell-handling claims.

canonical_name: Nguyen & Wereley 2006 — Fundamentals and Applications of Microfluidics (2nd ed) (textbook)
creator: Nam-Trung Nguyen, Steven T. Wereley
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-1580539722; Artech House, 2nd edition, 2006 (1st ed 2002)
prior_art_notes: Engineering textbook with extensive device-level coverage: micropumps (electrokinetic, piezo, peristaltic, thermopneumatic, MHD), microvalves (active and passive, check, pinch, ball), micromixers (passive lamination, chaotic advection, active acoustic and electrokinetic), and detection. Each device class is described in enough engineering detail to enable an undergraduate to build it. Anticipates: device-level patent claims on microfluidic pumps, valves, and mixers in any of the listed taxonomies — they are obvious in view of this textbook's catalog. Particularly load-bearing: catalog of 'pump architectures usable on chip' defeats narrow novelty for any post-2002 micropump claim.

canonical_name: Paper-based microfluidic devices for distributed point-of-care diagnostics
creator: Whitesides group, Harvard
disclosure_citation: Martinez, A. W.; Phillips, S. T.; Butte, M. J.; Whitesides, G. M. Patterned paper as a platform for inexpensive, low-volume, portable bioassays. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2007, 46, 1318–1320. DOI: 10.1002/anie.200603817
prior_art_notes: The paper that established paper-based microfluidic analytical devices (µPADs) as a category. Anticipates: hydrophobic patterning of cellulose paper to define fluid channels, capillary-driven flow without external pumps, multiplex colorimetric assays on a single paper substrate. The entire low-resource diagnostic paper-fluidics field descends from this disclosure.

canonical_name: Continuous inertial focusing, ordering, and separation of particles in microchannels
creator: Di Carlo, Toner et al. (Harvard / Mass General)
disclosure_citation: Di Carlo, D.; Irimia, D.; Tompkins, R. G.; Toner, M. Continuous inertial focusing, ordering, and separation of particles in microchannels. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 2007, 104, 18892–18897. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.0704958104
prior_art_notes: Established inertial microfluidics as a continuous-flow particle-separation regime exploiting Dean drag and shear-gradient lift in curving and straight channels at intermediate Reynolds numbers (Re~10–100). Anticipates: spiral and serpentine inertial focusing geometries, label-free CTC enrichment by inertial migration, sheath-free particle ordering, and the entire inertial-microfluidics subfield as commercialized by Vortex Biosciences, ClearCell, and the iCellate / iChip CTC platforms. Together with Sturm/Huang DLD (2004) it defines the dominant label-free continuous-separation paradigms.

canonical_name: Free-flow acoustophoresis for cell separation
creator: Laurell group, Lund University
disclosure_citation: Petersson, F.; Åberg, L.; Swärd-Nilsson, A.-M.; Laurell, T. Free flow acoustophoresis: microfluidic-based mode of particle and cell separation. Anal. Chem. 2007, 79, 5117–5123. DOI: 10.1021/ac070444e
prior_art_notes: Foundational disclosure of free-flow acoustophoresis: continuous-flow particle separation in a microchannel by transverse acoustic radiation force from a half-wavelength bulk acoustic standing wave, with sample inlet and multiple outlets at distinct lateral positions. Anticipates: silicon-channel BAW resonator architecture, label-free continuous acoustic separation by particle compressibility / density contrast, and the entire bulk-acoustic-wave acoustofluidics field commercialized by AcouSort and used in dozens of academic CTC and exosome platforms.

canonical_name: The origins and the future of microfluidics
creator: George Whitesides, Harvard
disclosure_citation: Whitesides, G. M. The origins and the future of microfluidics. Nature 2006, 442, 368–373. DOI: 10.1038/nature05058
prior_art_notes: Whitesides's history-and-prospects review identifying the four progenitor fields of microfluidics (analytical chemistry, biodefense, molecular biology, microelectronics). Cited as the standard origin-story reference. Does not disclose new devices but establishes the field's intellectual genealogy.

canonical_name: Acoustically detectable cellular-level lung injury model
creator: Takayama group, Michigan
disclosure_citation: Huh, D.; Fujioka, H.; Tung, Y.-C.; Futai, N.; Paine, R., 3rd; Grotberg, J. B.; Takayama, S. Acoustically detectable cellular-level lung injury induced by fluid mechanical stresses in microfluidic airway systems. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 2007, 104, 18886–18891. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.0610868104
prior_art_notes: Direct precursor to the Huh-Ingber 2010 lung-on-chip paper; demonstrated airway-stress modeling in PDMS chips. Establishes the Takayama-group lineage that connects to Ingber's Wyss Institute lung-on-chip and ultimately Emulate's commercial platform. Important for tracing the academic-to-commercial pathway of organ-on-chip work.

canonical_name: Microfluidic bubble logic
creator: Prakash, Gershenfeld (MIT)
disclosure_citation: Prakash, M.; Gershenfeld, N. Microfluidic bubble logic. Science 2007, 315, 832–835. DOI: 10.1126/science.1136907
prior_art_notes: Disclosed microfluidic bubble logic gates: AND/OR/NOT operations implemented purely in two-phase flow geometry, using bubbles as the binary signal. Anticipates: programmable microfluidic logic without electrical actuation, and the broader concept of fluidic-Turing-completeness on chip. Precursor of HUVAS-style bubble computers.

canonical_name: Bead-based cell capture in microfluidic channels
creator: Toner group, Mass General Hospital
disclosure_citation: Toner, M.; Irimia, D. Blood-on-a-chip. Annu. Rev. Biomed. Eng. 2005, 7, 77–103. DOI: 10.1146/annurev.bioeng.7.011205.135108
prior_art_notes: Toner-group review consolidating the 'blood-on-a-chip' research program: integrated separation, capture, and analysis of blood components on microfluidic chips. Cited as the canonical review for chip-format hematology and CTC isolation work; precursor to the CTC-iChip lineage.

canonical_name: Microfluidic alginate microbead generation
creator: various — Lee, Weitz, Doyle (early 2000s contributions)
disclosure_citation: Choi, C.-H.; Jung, J.-H.; Rhee, Y. W.; Kim, D.-P.; Shim, S.-E.; Lee, C.-S. Generation of monodisperse alginate microbeads and in situ encapsulation of cell in microfluidic device. Biomed. Microdevices 2007, 9, 855–862. DOI: 10.1007/s10544-007-9098-7
prior_art_notes: Foundational disclosure of microfluidic alginate microbead generation: aqueous alginate flow-focused into oil with downstream calcium-mediated gelation produces monodisperse alginate microbeads suitable for cell encapsulation. Anticipates: alginate-as-microbead-substrate-in-droplet-microfluidics, which became the backbone of single-cell sequencing platforms (Drop-seq, inDrops, Tapestri) where the bead encapsulates barcoding oligos.

Paper 2007-01-3142 (2007)

canonical_name: Bonn et al. 2009 - Wetting and spreading (Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 739)
creator: Daniel Bonn; Jens Eggers; Joseph Indekeu; Jacques Meunier; Etienne Rolley
disclosure_citation: Bonn, D., Eggers, J., Indekeu, J., Meunier, J., Rolley, E. (2009). 'Wetting and spreading.' Rev. Mod. Phys. 81(2): 739-805. doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.739
notable_capabilities: comprehensive RMP review of static and dynamic wetting
detailed treatment of contact-line motion, contact-angle hysteresis, partial-wetting
review-level reference for all surface-energy-driven microfluidics

canonical_name: Lung-on-a-chip
channel_geometry: two parallel PDMS channels separated by a thin porous membrane with cyclic pneumatic stretch
creator: Donald Ingber group, Wyss Institute
disclosure_citation: Huh, D.; Matthews, B. D.; Mammoto, A.; Montoya-Zavala, M.; Hsin, H. Y.; Ingber, D. E. Reconstituting organ-level lung functions on a chip. Science 2010, 328, 1662–1668. DOI: 10.1126/science.1188302
prior_art_notes: The foundational organ-on-chip disclosure: lung alveolar-capillary interface reconstituted on a microfluidic chip with cyclic mechanical stretch. Anticipates: dual-channel architecture with intervening porous membrane, mechanical actuation of cell-bearing membranes via pneumatic chambers, perfused human cell co-culture with epithelial-endothelial interfaces. Spawned the Emulate Inc. commercial platform and the entire organ-on-chip field.

canonical_name: Single molecule arrays (Simoa) for ultrasensitive immunoassay
creator: Walt group, Tufts / Quanterix
disclosure_citation: Rissin, D. M. et al. Single-molecule enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay detects serum proteins at subfemtomolar concentrations. Nat. Biotechnol. 2010, 28, 595–599. DOI: 10.1038/nbt.1641
prior_art_notes: Disclosed single-molecule immunoassay (Simoa): trap individual antibody-functionalized beads in femtoliter microwells, isolate by oil overlay to digitize fluorogenic-substrate signal per bead. Anticipates: femtoliter-microwell-array architecture for digital ELISA, oil-isolated chamber arrays for single-molecule chemistry, and the Quanterix HD-X / SR-X commercial platforms. Sub-femtomolar protein detection in serum.

canonical_name: Latching microfluidic valves and digital logic
creator: Quake / Horowitz groups, Stanford
disclosure_citation: Weaver, J. A.; Melin, J.; Stark, D.; Quake, S. R.; Horowitz, M. A. Static control logic for microfluidic devices using pressure-gain valves. Nat. Phys. 2010, 6, 218–223. DOI: 10.1038/nphys1513
prior_art_notes: Disclosed pressure-gain microfluidic valves enabling combinational logic on chip — microfluidic equivalents of CMOS logic gates. Demonstrates 8-bit shift register and ring oscillator implemented in PDMS. Anticipates: microfluidic-only digital control logic without external addressing electronics, and the architectural goal of a self-contained programmable chip without electronic peripherals.

canonical_name: Fluidic rectifier and microfluidic memory
creator: Takayama group, Michigan
disclosure_citation: Mosadegh, B.; Kuo, C.-H.; Tung, Y.-C.; Torisawa, Y.; Bersano-Begey, T.; Tavana, H.; Takayama, S. Integrated elastomeric components for autonomous regulation of sequential and oscillatory flow switching in microfluidic devices. Nat. Phys. 2010, 6, 433–437. DOI: 10.1038/nphys1637
prior_art_notes: Disclosed elastomeric fluidic-rectifier and oscillator primitives implemented as monolithic-PDMS Quake-valve variants. Provides a microfluidic equivalent of the diode and the relaxation oscillator. Anticipates: monolithic elastomeric fluidic logic substrate, and autonomous-pumping microfluidic chips that operate without external pressure modulation.

canonical_name: Mother machine: high-throughput single-bacterium tracking
creator: Jun group, UCSD
disclosure_citation: Wang, P.; Robert, L.; Pelletier, J.; Dang, W. L.; Taddei, F.; Wright, A.; Jun, S. Robust growth of Escherichia coli. Curr. Biol. 2010, 20, 1099–1103. DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2010.04.045
prior_art_notes: The 'mother machine': arrays of dead-end channels each holding a single bacterium with daughter cells flushed downstream. Enables thousands of independent single-cell lineage observations in parallel. Anticipates: dead-end-channel single-bacterium trap array architecture, time-resolved bacterial physiology measurements at scale, and the broader category of microfluidic devices for systematic bacterial physiology that became central in microbial-aging and antibiotic-resistance research.

canonical_name: Synthetic biology / circuit-design tools (microfluidics-relevant)

prior_art_notes: Synthesizing review of synthetic biology applications, with particular relevance to microfluidic chassis: every Synthetic-Biology platform that combines designer cells with microfluidic device-level control depends on integrating chip-format infrastructure with engineered genetic circuits. Methodological reference for the broader synthetic-biology + microfluidics intersection.

canonical_name: Ingber lab organ-chip platform (Wyss Institute)
creator: Ingber group, Wyss Institute / Harvard
disclosure_citation: Huh, D.; Hamilton, G. A.; Ingber, D. E. From 3D cell culture to organs-on-chips. Trends Cell Biol. 2011, 21, 745–754. DOI: 10.1016/j.tcb.2011.09.005
prior_art_notes: Wyss-Institute consolidating publication establishing the 'organ-on-chip' research program — direct architectural and IP ancestor of the Emulate Inc. commercial platform. Ingber group's organ-chip lineage covers lung-on-chip (Huh 2010), gut-on-chip, kidney-on-chip, blood-brain-barrier-on-chip and others, all sharing the dual-channel PDMS architecture with vacuum-driven mechanical strain.

canonical_name: Smartphone-based microscopy and microfluidic imaging (Ozcan 2010)
creator: Ozcan group, UCLA
disclosure_citation: Tseng, D.; Mudanyali, O.; Oztoprak, C.; Isikman, S. O.; Sencan, I.; Yaglidere, O.; Ozcan, A. Lensfree microscopy on a cellphone. Lab Chip 2010, 10, 1787–1792. DOI: 10.1039/C003477B
prior_art_notes: Foundational disclosure of smartphone-based lensless holographic microscopy for chip imaging: a sample on a microfluidic chip is illuminated by an LED placed atop a smartphone camera, producing a holographic shadow that is computationally reconstructed into an image. Anticipates: smartphone-as-microscope architecture for field-deployable microfluidic diagnostics, lensless computational imaging on chip, and the entire smartphone-based POC imaging subfield. Underlies dozens of subsequent academic and commercial efforts (Cellscope, Nuralogix, Ozcan-spinout commercial products).

canonical_name: Color-changing diagnostic paper microfluidics (multiple groups)
creator: Yetisen, Lowe (Cambridge)
disclosure_citation: Yetisen, A. K.; Akram, M. S.; Lowe, C. R. Paper-based microfluidic point-of-care diagnostic devices. Lab Chip 2013, 13, 2210–2251. DOI: 10.1039/C3LC50169H
prior_art_notes: Comprehensive review of paper-based microfluidic POC diagnostics: wax printing, hydrophobic patterning, multi-zone reagent staging, smartphone-camera readout. Cited as the standard reference for the entire paper-microfluidic POC subfield post-2010. Methodological complement to Whitesides foundational work and the Carrilho 2009 wax-printing recipe.

canonical_name: µPADs II / III: Systematic Whitesides disclosures

prior_art_notes: Systematic Whitesides-group disclosures extending µPAD architecture from the 2007 foundational disclosure: 3D µPADs (multi-layer paper assembly), electrochemical µPADs (printed electrodes on paper), µPADs with fluorescence detection. Cumulative Whitesides-group µPAD patent filings cover much of the broader paper-microfluidic patent landscape.
sources: Various Whitesides group µPAD II / III papers

prior_art_notes: Stanford/Quake-group patent family on bead-in-droplet single-cell barcoding. Anchors claims around: (a) microfluidic flow-focusing co-encapsulation of a single cell with a single barcoded primer-bearing bead in an oil-in-water droplet; (b) bead-bound oligonucleotide barcodes with cell-barcode + UMI + capture-sequence regions; (c) in-droplet lysis followed by mRNA capture on the bead; (d) bulk recovery of beads for downstream pooled library construction. Macosko 2015 Drop-seq (macosko-2015-drop-seq) is the publication-disclosure analog using the Broad/McCarroll lineage; this entry maps the licensable Stanford patent estate that 10x Genomics used as one input for the Chromium platform. Anticipates single-cell sequencing prep cartridges that use co-encapsulation of cell+bead in droplets.

canonical_name: Mark, Haeberle, Roth, von Stetten & Zengerle 2010 — Microfluidic lab-on-a-chip platforms
creator: Daniel Mark, Stefan Haeberle, Günter Roth, Felix von Stetten, Roland Zengerle
prior_art_notes: Critical Chem Soc Rev cataloguing the seven dominant microfluidic platforms by 2010: capillary, pressure-driven, centrifugal, electrokinetic, acoustic, free-flow, and droplet/digital. For each it lists fabrication, fluidic operations achievable, and example applications — i.e., a public engineering manual. Anticipates: any post-2010 patent that claims a 'microfluidic platform' architecturally indistinguishable from one of these seven (e.g., 'a centrifugal disc with siphon valves and detection chamber') as obvious in view of the Mark 2010 enumeration. Particularly load-bearing for centrifugal and droplet platform genus claims.

canonical_name: Qin, Xia & Whitesides 2010 / Nature Reviews Materials 2017 — soft lithography 20-year retrospective
creator: Dong Qin, Younan Xia, George M. Whitesides
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1038/nprot.2009.234; Nat. Protoc. 5, 491-502 (2010); plus Nature Reviews Materials retrospective volume 2 (2017) doi:10.1038/natrevmats.2017.16 'Three decades of microfluidics'
prior_art_notes: Comprehensive Nature Protocols + Nature Reviews Materials retrospectives that aggregate the soft-lithography toolkit (replica molding, microcontact printing, micromolding in capillaries, solvent-assisted micromolding) into a single citable disclosure. Anticipates: any patent claiming a fabrication process consisting of 'replica-molding a PDMS device against a photolithographically defined master' as obvious in view of the reviewed methods. Standard examiner reference for soft-litho 102/103.

canonical_name: Kirby 2010 — Micro- and Nanoscale Fluid Mechanics: Transport in Microfluidic Devices (textbook)
creator: Brian J. Kirby
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-0521119030; Cambridge University Press, 2010
prior_art_notes: Comprehensive engineering textbook on micro- and nanoscale fluid transport with emphasis on electrokinetics, electroosmosis, electrophoresis, dielectrophoresis, and species transport. Treats Debye layer physics, Smoluchowski slip, zeta-potential measurement, and electrokinetic separations. Anticipates: claims to electrokinetic microfluidic separators, ion-selective nanofluidic devices, and electrophoretic concentration platforms whose operating principle is a textbook derivation. The book's chapter on ion concentration polarization predates many later patents on ICP-based desalination and preconcentration.

canonical_name: Ion Torrent semiconductor sequencing chip
creator: Rothberg et al., Ion Torrent / Life Technologies
disclosure_citation: Rothberg, J. M. et al. An integrated semiconductor device enabling non-optical genome sequencing. Nature 2011, 475, 348–352. DOI: 10.1038/nature10242
prior_art_notes: Disclosed semiconductor sequencing: a CMOS chip with millions of pH-sensitive microwells, each with a single template-loaded bead, where polymerase-incorporation H+ release is detected by ISFET sensing. Architecturally a hybrid silicon-microfluidic-MEMS-CMOS device. Anticipates: integrated CMOS-fluidic sequencing, ISFET-array-as-sensor architecture, and the entire 'sequencing-on-a-chip' family that subsequently expanded to Roche 454, ONT MinION, PacBio, Element Biosciences AVITI, Singular Genomics G4.

canonical_name: Microfluidic bioreactor for individual yeast cells
creator: Heinemann, Lee labs (ETH / Berkeley)
disclosure_citation: Lee, S. S.; Avalos Vizcarra, I.; Huberts, D. H. E. W.; Lee, L. P.; Heinemann, M. Whole lifespan microscopic observation of budding yeast aging through a microfluidic dissection platform. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 2012, 109, 4916–4920. DOI: 10.1073/pnas.1113505109
prior_art_notes: Microfluidic device for whole-lifespan single-yeast-cell observation: cells trapped in posts that retain mother cells while flushing daughter cells, allowing 50+ cell-division observations without moving the trap. Anticipates: lifespan-tracking microfluidic single-cell traps, used widely in aging research and in synthetic-biology dynamics measurement.

canonical_name: OSTE (off-stoichiometry thiol-ene) microfluidic substrates
creator: van der Wijngaart, Carlborg, Haraldsson (KTH Stockholm)
disclosure_citation: Carlborg, C. F.; Haraldsson, T.; Öberg, K.; Malkoch, M.; van der Wijngaart, W. Beyond PDMS: off-stoichiometry thiol-ene (OSTE) based soft lithography for rapid prototyping of microfluidic devices. Lab Chip 2011, 11, 3136–3147. DOI: 10.1039/C1LC20388F
prior_art_notes: Disclosed OSTE (off-stoichiometry thiol-ene) substrate for microfluidics: a tunable photopolymer with controllable surface chemistry, mechanical properties, and bonding behavior. The OSTE+ variant adds reactive surface chemistry that allows direct chemical bonding to other substrates. Architectural alternative to PDMS for chips needing tuned surface chemistry, organic-solvent compatibility, and rigid mechanical properties.

canonical_name: GSK / CMAC Strathclyde continuous-flow API manufacturing platform
channel_geometry: Continuous synthesis suite: tubular PFR + MSMPR continuous crystallizer + continuous filter-dryer + continuous formulation; suite footprint ~80 m²; throughput up to 200 kg/day API
creator: Centre for Innovative Manufacturing in Continuous Manufacturing and Crystallisation (CMAC), University of Strathclyde, in collaboration with GSK and 7 pharma companies
disclosure_citation: Florence, A. J.; Johnston, A.; Price, S. L.; Nowell, H.; Kennedy, A. R.; Shankland, K. EPSRC Centre for Innovative Manufacturing in Continuous Manufacturing and Crystallisation (CMAC) launch, University of Strathclyde, 2011; Cole, K. P. et al. 'Kilogram-scale prexasertib monolactate monohydrate synthesis under continuous-flow CGMP conditions' Science 2017, 356, 1144–1150 (Eli Lilly + CMAC collaboration); CMAC Hub annual report 2015–2020
notable_capabilities: Industry-academic consortium continuous-API development platform
Demonstrated kilogram-scale CGMP continuous synthesis (prexasertib, Lilly 2017)
Full continuous-crystallization-control PAT (FBRM, Raman, particle vision)
Tier-1 pharma partners: GSK, Lilly, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Novartis, J&J, Roche
notes: CMAC was originally an EPSRC Innovative Manufacturing Centre (£10M, 2011) and was extended as the EPSRC Future Manufacturing Research Hub (£10M, 2017–2024). Eli Lilly's prexasertib production at Tippecanoe Indiana is a direct industrial deployment of CMAC methodology.
prior_art_notes: CMAC is the principal UK academic-industrial vehicle for continuous-API process development. Discloses (a) the canonical 'continuous-from-step-1-to-API' process map for small-molecule drug substance manufacturing; (b) continuous MSMPR cascade crystallization with PAT-driven control; (c) kg-scale CGMP-grade continuous flow demonstrated in the published Lilly prexasertib paper (Science 2017); (d) the consortium model in which 7 pharma companies share IP and process methods through the CMAC framework. Anticipates many process-method claims directed to 'continuous synthesis-crystallization-isolation of [small molecule API]' that have begun to appear in pharma patent literature 2018–2024.

canonical_name: Israelachvili 2011 - Intermolecular and Surface Forces (3rd ed.)
creator: Jacob N. Israelachvili

notable_capabilities: unified treatment of van der Waals, electric-double-layer, hydration, hydrophobic, and steric forces

load-bearing for nanofluidic and surface-functionalized microfluidic theory

prior_art_notes: Israelachvili textbook is the standard reference for intermolecular and surface forces, covering van der Waals interactions, electric-double-layer forces (extending DLVO from Verwey-Overbeek 1948), hydration and hydrophobic forces, and steric and bridging forces. Anticipates microfluidic claims involving surface-force-controlled nanochannel transport, particle-surface adhesion in microfluidic separations, and bio-functionalized surface-affinity capture in lab-on-chip cartridges. Any patent claiming novelty around tunable surface-interaction forces in microfluidics must clear Israelachvili.

notable_capabilities: comprehensive RMP review of acoustofluidic theory and devices
SAW, BAW, and acoustic-streaming microfluidic applications
mass-transfer and atomization at the microscale

Anticipates any patent claim around SAW-driven, BAW-driven, or acoustic-streaming microfluidic devices. Required clearance for the entire acoustofluidic patent ecosystem.

canonical_name: Friend & Yeo SAW Microfluidics Review
creator: James Friend & Leslie Yeo (RMIT/Monash)
disclosure_citation: Friend J., Yeo L. Y., Reviews of Modern Physics 83, 647 (2011), doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.83.647
notable_capabilities: taxonomic survey of standing-SAW vs travelling-SAW manipulation
droplet translation, atomization, jetting, mixing
interdigital transducer geometry conventions
prior_art_notes: This Reviews of Modern Physics article codifies the field of surface-acoustic-wave (SAW) microfluidics, providing element-by-element disclosures of: (a) interdigital transducer (IDT) layouts on Y-cut/X-propagating lithium niobate for Rayleigh SAW generation; (b) acoustic streaming inside sessile droplets via leaky-SAW coupling; (c) standing-SAW pressure-node manipulation of particles in microchannels coupled to PDMS overlays; (d) SAW-driven atomization for nebulizer applications. Anticipates broad downstream patent claims to IDT-driven droplet manipulation, SAW pumping, and SAW-induced acoustic streaming for mixing or particle focusing in PDMS-on-LiNbO3 hybrid devices. Provides 102 disclosure for any combination of these elements claimed after April 2011.

canonical_name: Madou 2011 — Fundamentals of Microfabrication and Nanotechnology (3rd ed, 3-volume) (textbook)
creator: Marc J. Madou
prior_art_notes: Three-volume engineering reference covering MEMS and microfluidic fabrication: photolithography, soft-lithography, hot embossing, injection molding, LIGA, deep RIE, glass etching, bonding (anodic, fusion, thermocompression, plasma), and integration. Volume III specifically covers manufacturing techniques for microfluidics. Anticipates: any patent on a 'method of fabricating a microfluidic device' that claims a process step (lithography, etch, mold, bond) that is documented in Madou's textbook before the patent priority date. Standard examiner reference for fabrication 102/103 rejections.

disclosure_citation: Mahaffy PR et al., 'The Sample Analysis at Mars Investigation and Instrument Suite,' Space Science Reviews 170:401-478 (2012), doi:10.1007/s11214-012-9879-z; Glavin DP et al., 'Evidence for perchlorates and the origin of chlorinated hydrocarbons detected by SAM at the Rocknest aeolian deposit in Gale Crater,' JGR Planets 118:1955-1973 (2013)
notable_capabilities: in-situ chemical derivatization of refractory polar organics (amino acids, carboxylic acids) on Mars
perchlorate-tolerant analytical chain via MTBSTFA silylation

notes: SAM is the most-cited in-situ planetary microfluidic instrument in the published literature. The wet-chemistry cup architecture predates Mars 2020 and ExoMars MOMA equivalents.
prior_art_notes: Discloses a sealed reagent-cup architecture for in-situ wet chemistry on a planetary surface: a metal cup with crimped foil seal containing premixed MTBSTFA/DMF derivatization reagent at flight-storage temperature; the cup is mechanically pierced (foil-pierce actuation analogous to terrestrial blister-pack diagnostics), the regolith aliquot is dropped in, and the cup is heated stepwise to release derivatized analytes into the GCMS gas train. For 102/103 anticipation: (a) the foil-pierce + sealed-reagent + thermal-release architecture anticipates any patent claiming a single-use derivatization cartridge for sample-prep before MS, (b) the use of MTBSTFA specifically for in-situ silylation of amino acids/carboxylic acids in the presence of perchlorate oxidizers anticipates Mars/Europa/Enceladus life-detection cartridges that propose perchlorate-tolerant derivatization, and (c) the carousel architecture with mixed wet-chem and pyrolysis-only cups anticipates multi-modal sample-prep cartridges. The post-flight realization that perchlorate combustion was destroying organics during pyrolysis (Glavin 2013) is itself prior art against any claim that perchlorate-mitigation derivatization is novel for astrobiology applications.
sample_volume: ~135 mm^3 of pre-sieved (<150 µm) regolith per cup; 1 µL-scale derivatization reagent volumes liberated upon cup heating
sensing: mass-spec coupled (quadrupole MS, m/z 2-535); 6-column tunable laser spectrometer; gas chromatograph (6 columns)
sources: Mahaffy PR et al., Space Sci Rev 170:401 (2012)
Glavin DP et al., JGR Planets 118:1955 (2013)
Freissinet C et al., 'Organic molecules in the Sheepbed Mudstone, Gale Crater, Mars,' JGR Planets 120:495-514 (2015)
Eigenbrode JL et al., 'Organic matter preserved in 3-billion-year-old mudstones at Gale crater, Mars,' Science 360:1096 (2018)

canonical_name: Mayo Collaborative Services v. Prometheus Laboratories 2012 (Diagnostic-Method Patentability)
creator: Supreme Court of the United States
notable_capabilities: narrowed Section 101 patent eligibility for diagnostic methods
applies to any microfluidic-cartridge claim that recites only natural correlations + conventional measurement
notes: Foundational case-law entry. 102/103 prior art is the wrong frame for case law; this entry is an enforceability-defense reference rather than novelty prior art. Categorized as `corpus: academic` (public-domain status captured in `ip_status`).
prior_art_notes: Case-law entry. Mayo v. Prometheus 566 U.S. 66 (2012) narrowed 35 USC Section 101 patent eligibility for diagnostic methods, holding that a claim reciting a natural correlation (here, between thiopurine metabolite levels and dosing) plus conventional measurement steps is not patent-eligible subject matter. Direct relevance to microfluidics: any cartridge-or-method patent that claims merely 'measure analyte X with my cartridge and infer condition Y' is at risk under Mayo. Combined with Myriad (gene patents) and Alice (software-implemented), forms the modern Section 101 trilogy. Defensive value: any microfluidic cartridge patent practitioner should evaluate Section 101 risk under Mayo before relying on broad diagnostic-correlation claims.
sources: Mayo Collaborative Services v. Prometheus Laboratories 566 U.S. 66 (2012)
USPTO subject matter eligibility guidance MPEP 2106

The CRISPR-Cas9 patent dispute between Broad Institute (Zhang lab) and UC Berkeley (Doudna/Charpentier) is the most-litigated biotech IP case of the 2010s-2020s. PTAB Interference No. 106,048 (declared 2016-01-11) and successor proceedings: Broad won eukaryotic-application priority (2017 PTAB, 2022 PTAB rehearing); UCB retained generic-prokaryotic priority. Direct relevance to microfluidics: microfluidic cartridges that perform CRISPR-Cas9 editing of eukaryotic cells (e.g., Aspara CRISPR detection, igem-epfl-2018-crispr-ctdna-microfluidics, igem-hkust-2020-crispr-cas13-detection, pasteur-crispr-cartridge-academic) face dual-licensing demand from both Broad and UCB. Patents subsequently licensed via Editas (Broad), Caribou (UCB), CRISPR Therapeutics (Charpentier), Intellia (Doudna). Defensive value: catalogs the multi-priority patent landscape any CRISPR-cartridge developer must navigate.
sources: Federal Circuit Broad v. UCB appeals 2018, 2022

canonical_name: Association for Molecular Pathology v. Myriad Genetics 2013 (Gene Patents Struck)

notes: Foundational case-law entry. Enabled an entire generation of competitive BRCA testing services. Categorized as `corpus: academic` (public-domain status captured in `ip_status`).
prior_art_notes: Case-law entry. AMP v. Myriad 569 U.S. 576 (2013) held that isolated naturally-occurring DNA sequences (the BRCA1/BRCA2 gene patents at issue) are not patent-eligible subject matter under Section 101 because they are products of nature. Synthetic cDNA remained patentable. Direct relevance to microfluidics: any cartridge-or-platform patent that depends in part on claims to natural nucleic-acid sequences is at risk. Defensive value: enables cartridges to detect BRCA / other natural sequences without licensing the (now-invalid) underlying gene patents. Combined with Mayo and Alice, defines the modern Section 101 narrowing.

disclosure_citation: Sollier, E. et al. Size-selective collection of circulating tumor cells using Vortex technology. Lab Chip 2014, 14, 63–77. DOI: 10.1039/C3LC50689D
prior_art_notes: Disclosed vortex-chamber inertial separation: large CTCs are trapped in microscale vortex chambers via inertial migration while smaller blood cells flow through, enabling label-free size-based CTC enrichment. Anticipates: vortex-chamber-as-cell-trap architecture, label-free CTC isolation by inertial trapping (distinct from inertial focusing for streamline ordering). Commercial implementation: Vortex Biosciences VTX-1 (now part of NanoString).

canonical_name: Microfluidic soil DNA extraction and pathogen detection
creator: Bridle group, Heriot-Watt
disclosure_citation: Bridle, H.; Miller, B.; Desmulliez, M. P. Y. Application of microfluidics in waterborne pathogen monitoring: a review. Water Res. 2014, 55, 256–271. DOI: 10.1016/j.watres.2014.01.061
prior_art_notes: Foundational review establishing microfluidic waterborne pathogen detection as a coherent subfield: integration of sample-prep (filtration, concentration), nucleic-acid extraction, isothermal amplification, and integrated detection on portable cartridges. Anticipates: water-quality cartridge architecture for field deployment, distinct from clinical POC cartridges by emphasizing large-volume sample concentration upstream of small-volume analytical chamber. Underlies subsequent commercial efforts by ALS Limited, IDEXX Colilert systems, and academic agricultural-water-quality startups.

canonical_name: Microfluidic extracellular vesicle / exosome isolation

canonical_name: WISSARD / SALSA Subglacial Antarctic Microbial Samplers

disclosure_citation: Christner BC et al., 'A microbial ecosystem beneath the West Antarctic ice sheet,' Nature 512:310-313 (2014), doi:10.1038/nature13667; Priscu JC et al., 'Scientific access into Mercer Subglacial Lake: scientific objectives, drilling operations and initial observations,' Annals of Glaciology 62:340-352 (2021)

Sterivex closed-cartridge filter format adopted as the de facto standard for clean subglacial sampling

notes: Direct terrestrial analog for Europa/Enceladus mission planning. WISSARD also pre-dates the more famous Subglacial Lake Vostok (Lake Vostok work was contamination-compromised and cannot be cited as clean prior art).
prior_art_notes: Discloses the cleanest-published terrestrial protocol for retrieving microbiologically-pristine subsurface aqueous samples — the most directly cited prior art for any future Europa/Enceladus subsurface life detection mission. Element-by-element: (a) hot-water drill with multi-stage HEPA + 0.2 µm filtration + UV-C sterilization of drill water anticipates patents claiming planetary subsurface drilling fluid sterilization architectures; (b) Sterivex closed-cartridge format with sealed inlet/outlet for downstream nucleic acid extraction without breaking sterility anticipates planetary sample-handling cartridges that must preserve sterility from sample-take through analysis; (c) the published clean-tent protocols and contamination-control budgets are open prior art that any 'planetary protection' patent would have to overcome. WISSARD/SALSA are the gold standard for terrestrial-analog subsurface-ocean sampling.
sample_volume: 10 L water samples filtered onto Sterivex membranes; subsequent 10 mL elution per cartridge for downstream sequencing
sensing: optical (epifluorescence DAPI counts on-site); off-site Illumina/PacBio sequencing
sources: Priscu JC et al., Annals of Glaciology 62:340 (2021)
Mikucki JA et al., 'Subglacial Lake Whillans microbial biogeochemistry: a synthesis of current knowledge,' Phil. Trans. Royal Soc. A 374:20140290 (2016)

canonical_name: Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International 2014 (Software/Abstract-Idea Patent Restriction)
creator: Supreme Court of the United States
notable_capabilities: narrowed patent eligibility for abstract ideas implemented on a computer
two-step Mayo/Alice test
applies to microfluidic-control software claims
notes: Foundational case-law entry. Significantly affects firmware/control-software-side patenting strategy for microfluidic instruments. Categorized as `corpus: academic` (public-domain status captured in `ip_status`).
prior_art_notes: Case-law entry. Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank 573 U.S. 208 (2014) extended Mayo to software patents, establishing the two-step Mayo/Alice test for Section 101 eligibility: (1) does the claim recite an abstract idea, law of nature, or natural phenomenon; (2) if so, does it add an inventive concept that transforms the claim into patent-eligible subject matter. Direct relevance to microfluidics: any patent claim to 'a microfluidic device with a controller that implements algorithm X' must avoid being a generic-computer-on-microfluidic-device claim. Defensive value: any microfluidic-control software patent (e.g., dPCR threshold-calling algorithms, droplet-detection algorithms, MLSI valve-scheduling software) is at risk under Alice. Combined with Mayo and Myriad, defines modern Section 101 limitations.
sources: Alice Corp. Pty. Ltd. v. CLS Bank International 573 U.S. 208 (2014)

canonical_name: Whitesides 2014 — Cool, or simple and cheap? Why not both?

canonical_name: Tony Jun Huang Lab Tunable Acoustic Tweezers
creator: Tony Jun Huang group (Penn State, later Duke)
notable_capabilities: tilted-angle SSAW separation by size

prior_art_notes: Discloses tilted-angle standing surface acoustic wave (taSSAW) chip wherein two opposing IDTs generate a standing wave at an angle to the flow direction; particles experience a pressure-gradient force that translates them across streamlines as a function of size and compressibility. Anticipates: (i) SSAW-based label-free cell sorters with continuous outflow; (ii) acoustic separators tuned by transducer angle rather than frequency; (iii) integration of taSSAW with downstream sequencing inputs (e.g., CTC enrichment). Companion to Ding 2012 acoustic-tweezer entry but adds productizable separation geometry.

canonical_name: Drop-seq single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: Macosko, McCarroll lab, Broad Institute
disclosure_citation: Macosko, E. Z. et al. Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets. Cell 2015, 161, 1202–1214. DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2015.05.002
prior_art_notes: Anticipates: co-encapsulation of single cells with barcoded beads in droplets via flow-focusing, lysis-on-bead chemistry, downstream pooled sequencing with barcode demultiplexing. Together with InDrops (Klein et al. 2015), this is the technical foundation of the modern single-cell genomics ecosystem, including the commercial 10x Genomics Chromium platform.

canonical_name: inDrops: droplet-based barcoding for single-cell transcriptomics
creator: Klein, Weitz, Kirschner labs (Harvard)
disclosure_citation: Klein, A. M.; Mazutis, L.; Akartuna, I.; Tallapragada, N.; Veres, A.; Li, V.; Peshkin, L.; Weitz, D. A.; Kirschner, M. W. Droplet barcoding for single-cell transcriptomics applied to embryonic stem cells. Cell 2015, 161, 1187–1201. DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2015.04.044
prior_art_notes: Published one week after Drop-seq; together they establish single-cell droplet RNA-seq as a category. inDrops uses hydrogel-encapsulated barcodes (rather than Drop-seq's polystyrene beads), an architectural choice subsequently inherited by 1Cell-Bio's commercial inDrops platform. Both papers anticipate: massively parallel single-cell RNA-seq via droplet co-encapsulation, but with different bead chemistries that anchor distinct patent positions.

canonical_name: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin MOMA (Mars Organic Molecule Analyser)
channel_geometry: 32-position sample carousel; 20 pyrolysis ovens (single-use), 8 derivatization ovens with MTBSTFA/DMF, 2 thermochemolysis ovens with TMAH; ~250 mg sample per oven; tapping-mode core sampling from 2 m subsurface drill
creator: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) / NASA GSFC / LISA / CNES / ESA / Thales Alenia Space
disclosure_citation: Goesmann F et al., 'The Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) Instrument: Characterization of Organic Material in Martian Sediments,' Astrobiology 17(6-7):655-685 (2017), doi:10.1089/ast.2016.1551
notable_capabilities: combined pyr-GCMS + LDMS in a single MS analyzer (ion-trap)
chiral GC columns for amino-acid enantiomer (D/L) discrimination as biosignature
LDI provides perchlorate-bypassing direct desorption of polyaromatic hydrocarbons
samples drawn from up to 2 m below Martian surface (Rosalind Franklin drill)
notes: Launch slipped from 2018 -> 2022 -> currently 2028 due to ExoMars program reset, but the instrument design and prior art are public-domain since 2017.
prior_art_notes: Discloses a hybrid pyrolysis/derivatization/laser-desorption mass-spec instrument with a 32-cell sealed-cup carousel architecture as in-situ sample prep. Element-by-element disclosure: (a) the dual-front-end design (thermal pyrolysis path + UV-LDI path sharing a single ion trap) anticipates patents claiming dual-mode MS sample introduction for planetary life detection; (b) the chiral-column GC train specifically targeting amino-acid enantiomer ratios as a life-detection signature anticipates terrestrial commercial chiral-LC/GC cartridges marketed for biosignature discrimination; (c) the 2-meter subsurface drill aliquot pathway with sealed transfer to a sample carousel anticipates concepts for Europa Lander / Enceladus subsurface sample acquisition; (d) the perchlorate-bypassing LDI ionization mode anticipates any patent claiming non-thermal direct laser ionization for Mars/icy-moon refractory organics. MOMA is the European/American sister architecture to SAM and the most current public-domain disclosure of an integrated pyr-GCMS-LDMS planetary cartridge.
sample_volume: ~2-30 mg sample subaliquot to GCMS train; ~10-50 µg LDMS spot
sensing: mass-spec coupled (linear ion trap MS, m/z 50-1000); pulsed UV laser desorption ionization (LDI) at 266 nm for refractory aromatics; 4-column GC (3 chiral, 1 polar)
sources: Vago JL et al., 'Habitability on Early Mars and the Search for Biosignatures with the ExoMars Rover,' Astrobiology 17:471 (2017)
Arevalo R et al., 'Design and demonstration of the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) on the ExoMars 2018 rover,' IEEE Aerospace Conf. (2015)
Li X et al., 'Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) laser desorption/ionization source design and performance characterization,' Int. J. Mass Spectrom. 422:177 (2017)
throughput: single-use ovens; 32-cell carousel total (different oven types)

canonical_name: Mars 2020 Perseverance MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment)
channel_geometry: Solid Oxide Electrolysis (SOXE) stack with 10 cells of scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte; 3D-printed superalloy gas-handling manifold; HEPA dust filter; CO2 inlet via scroll compressor at ~1 atm to feed cathode
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory / MIT Haystack / Niels Bohr Institute / OxEon Energy
disclosure_citation: Hecht MH et al., 'Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE),' Space Science Reviews 217:9 (2021), doi:10.1007/s11214-020-00782-8; Hoffman JA et al., 'Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE)—preparing for human Mars exploration,' Science Advances 8:eabp8636 (2022)
ip_citations: US20180023202A1 (NASA application on solid-oxide electrolysis cell stack design — prosecution status varies)
notable_capabilities: first in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) demonstration on another planet
solid-oxide electrochemistry at 800 C in a flight cartridge with scroll compressor pre-stage
feedback-controlled current/voltage operation across day/night Mars atmospheric pressure swings (4-9 mbar)
3D-printed Inconel manifold with integrated channels and getter pre-treatment
notes: Patent landscape around solid-oxide cell architecture is dense (OxEon, Ceramatec, Bloom Energy). MOXIE flight is public domain prior art for spaceflight integration.
prior_art_notes: Discloses an integrated gas-fluidic cartridge architecture for planetary in-situ resource utilization: (a) scroll-compressor + HEPA particulate filter + 3D-printed superalloy manifold + solid-oxide electrolyzer stack + getter scrubber; (b) the gas-handling subsystem operates as a flow-controlled, feedback-loop system with mass-flow sensors at inlet and oxygen-purity sensors at the anode-side outlet. For 102/103 anticipation: the assembly anticipates patents on integrated planetary atmospheric processing cartridges that combine compression, filtration, electrolysis, and getter purification on a single thermally-managed substrate. The 3D-printed manifold subsystem (additively-manufactured Inconel internal flow paths) is itself prior art against any patent claiming additively-manufactured high-temperature gas-flow manifolds for spaceflight chemical reactors. The stack-level current-voltage feedback control across diurnal pressure variations anticipates closed-loop control patents for variable-input ISRU systems.
sample_volume: ingests Mars atmosphere (96% CO2) at ~14 g/hr; produces ~6-10 g O2/hr
sensing: mass-flow controllers, electrochemical impedance, in-line oxygen partial pressure sensor
sources: Hecht MH et al., Space Sci Rev 217:9 (2021)
Hoffman JA et al., Science Advances 8:eabp8636 (2022)
throughput: 10+ g O2 per 1-hour run; 16 successful runs across Mars Year 36-37

canonical_name: OSIRIS-REx TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism)
channel_geometry: Sample head: ~30 cm diameter chamber with annular nitrogen gas-purge ports that fluidize regolith into the collector during a ~5 second touch-and-go contact; Velcro-pad surface contact pads on the bottom; sealed with O-ring on retraction
creator: Lockheed Martin Space / NASA Goddard / University of Arizona (D. Lauretta PI)
disclosure_citation: Bierhaus EB et al., 'The OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft and the Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism (TAGSAM),' Space Science Reviews 214:107 (2018), doi:10.1007/s11214-018-0521-6; Lauretta DS et al., 'Asteroid (101955) Bennu in the laboratory: Properties of the sample collected by OSIRIS-REx,' Meteoritics & Planetary Science 59:2453 (2024)
notable_capabilities: nitrogen-jet-fluidized regolith capture mechanism (active gas-purge sampling)
first US asteroid sample return mission; sample arrived Sept 2023
demonstrated controlled-atmosphere capture of friable carbonaceous chondrite material
TAGSAM head canister enables nominal 1 atm N2 storage of pristine sample for return
notes: Bennu sample showed evidence of phyllosilicates, organics including amino acids and nucleobases. The disclosed gas-fluidization fluidic mechanism is the relevant microfluidics-corpus content.
prior_art_notes: The TAGSAM head is a gas-fluidized sample acquisition cartridge — relevant to the microfluidics corpus as a non-canonical fluidic system: pressurized N2 jets fluidize asteroid regolith into the collection chamber, then the chamber is sealed with an O-ring against contamination. Element-by-element prior art for: (a) gas-fluidized loose-particulate sampling cartridges with sealed return architecture (anticipates terrestrial industrial fluid-bed dry-sample collectors and bio-aerosol capture cartridges); (b) the integration of multiple sample-capture methods on one head (gas jets + Velcro contact pads) anticipates patents claiming hybrid dry-sampling cartridges; (c) the curation chain from in-flight sealed canister -> Earth-return capsule -> JSC nitrogen glove-box curation establishes a published cleanroom protocol for friable carbonaceous samples that anticipates Mars Sample Return curation patents. Patent citation is for the Lockheed-developed sample capture architecture.
sample_volume: design target 60 g / minimum success 60 g / actual collected 121.6 g of Bennu regolith
sensing: mass-on-arm via spacecraft inertial properties; visible/IR imaging during contact
sources: Bierhaus EB et al., Space Sci Rev 214:107 (2018)
Lauretta DS et al., 'OSIRIS-REx asteroid sample collection: Decadal-class achievement,' AGU 2023 abstracts

canonical_name: Mathies/Quinn 2017 Microchip Capillary Electrophoresis for Mars Amino Acid Detection
channel_geometry: Glass microchip CE separation channel ~25 cm; LIF detection downstream; integrated programmable membrane microvalve array (Quake-style PDMS-on-glass) for sample dilution, fluorescent labeling with Pacific Blue or fluorescamine, and injection into the CE channel
creator: Richard Mathies group (UC Berkeley) / Peter Willis (NASA JPL) / Maria Mora (NASA JPL) / Aaron Noell
disclosure_citation: Mora MF et al., 'Toward total automation of microfluidics for extraterrestrial in situ analysis,' Anal. Chem. 83:8636 (2011); Mora MF et al. (Mathies/Quinn group), 'Capillary electrophoresis amino acid sensitivity from a chip-based instrument,' Electrophoresis 38:2982 (2017), doi:10.1002/elps.201700110
notable_capabilities: first sub-ppb amino acid detection in a flight-prototype microchip CE for Mars/icy moons
integrated programmable PDMS-on-glass valve array for full sample preparation (extraction + labeling + injection) on chip
chiral separation capability for D/L amino acid biosignature detection
directly proposed as instrument payload for ELSAH (Enceladus Life Signatures and Habitability) and other concept missions
notes: Lineage ancestor: skelley-2009-cell-pairing-trap (separate Mathies-group entry); also cited as the prior art for any future Enceladus/Mars amino acid microfluidic cartridge.
prior_art_notes: The Mathies/Quinn line of work is the most extensively-published academic flight-prototype for microfluidic life detection on Mars and icy moons. Element-by-element prior art: (a) the integration of programmable PDMS-on-glass membrane valves with on-chip CE separation for extraterrestrial sample analysis anticipates any patent claiming integrated sample-prep + electrophoretic-separation + LIF cartridges for planetary instruments; (b) the published parts-per-trillion sensitivity for fluorescamine-labeled amino acids in a portable / battery-powered instrument anticipates patents claiming similar sensitivity in handheld biosensors; (c) chiral separation as a biosignature-discrimination strategy on a microchip CE format anticipates any patent claiming D/L enantiomer microfluidic separation for biosignature detection. The Mora 2011/2017 papers also disclose the architectural pattern of a fully-automated 'Mars Organic Analyzer' (MOA) cartridge.
sample_volume: ~10 nL injected onto the CE channel from ~10 µL processed sample
sensing: fluorescence-on-chip (LIF with Pacific Blue / fluorescamine derivatization)
sources: Mora MF et al., Anal Chem 83:8636 (2011)

Skelley AM, Mathies RA, 'Chiral separation of fluorescamine-labeled amino acids using microfabricated capillary electrophoresis devices for extraterrestrial exploration,' J. Chromatogr. A 1021:191 (2003)
Willis PA et al., 'Investigation of microfluidic sample preparation for the SOLID life-detection instrument,' LPSC 41 (2010)
throughput: single CE run, 10-20 minutes; ~100 ppt (parts-per-trillion) amino acid LOD

Microfluidic-relevant element is parylene encapsulation as ECF barrier.

canonical_name: Mars 2020 Perseverance SHERLOC (Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals)
channel_geometry: no fluidic channels per se; arm-mounted instrument addresses a 7x7 mm region with 100 µm laser spot; calibration target carries 5 organic/mineral standards including spacesuit-fabric witness samples
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory / Photon Systems Inc. (deep-UV laser)
disclosure_citation: Bhartia R et al., 'Perseverance's Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman and Luminescence for Organics and Chemicals (SHERLOC) Investigation,' Space Science Reviews 217:58 (2021), doi:10.1007/s11214-021-00812-z; Beegle LW et al., '2018 SHERLOC instrument briefing'
notable_capabilities: first deep-UV Raman spectrometer on another planet
fluorescence-Raman dual-mode resonance enhancement for aromatic biosignatures (single-molecule sensitivity for PAHs)

no sample contact / no sample handling — purely standoff at 48 mm working distance
notes: Paired with PIXL (separate entry) as the Mars 2020 'arm-mounted micro-investigation' duo. SHERLOC's calibration target spacesuit-witness samples are themselves a quietly-important prior art disclosure for astronaut life-support polymer qualification.
prior_art_notes: Although SHERLOC has minimal classical fluidics, it is a load-bearing prior art entry for the broader 'in-situ life detection' patent landscape because it discloses (a) a deep-UV resonance-Raman + native-fluorescence dual-mode standoff cartridge architecture as an alternative to wet-chemistry GCMS for organic detection, (b) a co-mounted optical micrometer (WATSON) providing context imaging for spectroscopic point picks, and (c) the use of polymer/fabric witness samples on the calibration target as a vehicle for additional in-flight prior-art disclosure (the spacesuit Vectran/polycarbonate samples become public-domain prior art for astronaut suit polymers by virtue of being launched). For invalidation purposes, SHERLOC anticipates any claim to a deep-UV (sub-260 nm) raster-Raman cartridge for biosignature detection or any claim to a combined Raman/LIF standoff astrobiology head with mineralogical context co-imaging.
sample_volume: interrogates a ~50 µm spot on rock surface; integrated WATSON microscope provides imaging context
sensing: deep-UV (248.6 nm) Raman and laser-induced fluorescence; resonance Raman cross-section enhancement for aromatics
sources: Bhartia R et al., Space Sci Rev 217:58 (2021)
Razzell Hollis J et al., 'PIXL and SHERLOC: complementary mineralogy/chemistry instruments,' LPSC 52 (2021)
Beegle LW et al., 'SHERLOC: Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman and Luminescence for Organics and Chemicals, an investigation for 2020,' IEEE Aerospace Conf. (2015)
